module_title: Advanced Framework - Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) & Employment Economics
introduction: Modern economics has moved beyond single monetary poverty lines to assess multidimensional deprivation. This tier covers the National MPI launched by NITI Aayog, the PLFS metrics for unemployment, and macroeconomic curves relating to joblessness.

core_concepts.title: Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)
core_concepts.description:
- **Publishers:** UNDP and OPHI (Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative).
- **Structure:** Measures deprivation across 3 equally weighted dimensions: **Health, Education, and Standard of Living**.
- **Indicators:** It uses exactly 10 indicators (e.g., child mortality, years of schooling, cooking fuel, sanitation, etc.).

core_concepts.title: National MPI (by NITI Aayog)
core_concepts.description:
- **Structure:** Retains the 3 dimensions of the Global MPI but adapts the indicators to the Indian context.
- **Indicators:** Uses **12 indicators**. NITI Aayog added two specific indicators: **Maternal Health** (under Health) and **Bank Account** (under Standard of Living) to align with national schemes like Jan Dhan Yojana.

core_concepts.title: Labor Force Metrics (PLFS)
core_concepts.description:
- **Labor Force Participation Rate (LFPR):** The percentage of the population that is either working or actively looking for work. (Excludes students, retirees, homemakers).
- **Worker Population Ratio (WPR):** The percentage of the population that is *actually* employed.
- **Unemployment Rate (UR):** The percentage of the *Labor Force* (not total population) that is unemployed.

core_concepts.title: Macroeconomic Unemployment Concepts
core_concepts.description:
- **Okun's Law:** States that there is an inverse relationship between unemployment and GDP growth (If GDP grows by a certain rate, unemployment will fall).
- **Phillips Curve:** Demonstrates an inverse relationship between the rate of unemployment and the rate of inflation (lower unemployment leads to higher wages and thus higher inflation).

important_entities.name: Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)
important_entities.significance: Launched in 2017 by the NSO (National Statistical Office). It replaced the old 5-year employment surveys to provide more frequent (quarterly for urban, annual for rural) data on LFPR, WPR, and UR.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Labor Force vs. Work Force Trap
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
In economics, these terms are strictly distinct:
- **Labor Force** = Employed + Unemployed (but actively seeking work).
- **Work Force** = ONLY those who are employed.
Therefore, Unemployment = Labor Force minus Work Force.

If a question asks 'Which of the following is NOT a dimension of the MPI?', students often guess incorrectly. **Income/Per Capita Income is NOT a dimension of the MPI**. The MPI measures deprivation through Health, Education, and Standard of Living indicators.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Moms and Money (Maternal Health + Bank Accounts)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: To remember the difference between Global MPI (10 indicators) and India's National MPI (12 indicators), just remember NITI Aayog added 'Moms' (Maternal Health) and 'Money' (Bank Accounts).

exam_strategy_tips: In UPSC Prelims and Tier-2 SSC exams, the components of the NITI Aayog MPI and the Phillips Curve are highly tested. Knowing that 'Bank Account' is an MPI indicator often helps in eliminating wrong options.
